title: Dynamic probe + rescale calibration workflow for quant profiles across Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a reproducible calibration workflow that probes the activation statistics per-model and dynamically computes per-layer rescale hooks to control extreme activation outliers for FP8/INT8 quant profiles. This ticket covers engineering the probe runner, a rescale policy engine, validation harness against ground-truth fp32 outputs, and a safe rollout path for Llama, Mistral and Qwen families.
background: Previous work reduced large-model quantization instability via static layer scaling and global clipping heuristics. Those mitigations did not generalize cleanly across Mistral and newer Qwen variants because activation distributions vary by tokenizer length and attention patterns. This causes tail outliers that break INT8/FP8 mapping and produce accuracy regressions for some model+prompt families.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement a lightweight 'probe runner' that samples representative micro-batches across token lengths and generation modes (prompt-only / chat / generation) and computes per-layer activation percentiles (1%, 99.9%), sparse max, and variance. 2) Derive a per-layer rescale factor using a constrained optimization heuristic: minimize L2 perturbation of weights subject to limiting activation peak-to-median ratio (configurable). 3) Store a model-specific quant profile (rescale hooks + clip thresholds) in the model manifest. 4) Integrate the rescale hooks at kernel-launch time in the runtime with a fast path for no-op when factor==1.0. 5) Provide an automated validation harness comparing fp32 reference outputs using pass/fail thresholds on token-level logprobs, top-k overlap and an eval-suite of downstream tasks.
implementation_notes: - Probe runner runs inside the calibration env and accepts a small corpus (<=1k tokens) from perf dataset. - Use streaming statistics (Welford) to avoid double memory for large layers. - Rescale operations will be fused to pre/post GEMM ops where possible to avoid memory copies. - Preserve deterministic seed for probe sampling. - Add feature flag 'quant.dynamic_rescale_v2' guarded by release gate.
experiments: Phase A: run probes on Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Qwen-14B for prompt-length buckets (<=32, 33-128, 128-512). Phase B: validate INT8/FP8 quant profiles with and without rescale on held-out evals: common sense QA, code generation subset, and our perf P99 latency harness. Early results (prototype): median logprob delta <0.02 and top-1 overlap recovery improved by 6% on Qwen examples that previously regressed. Latency overhead of rescale fused path ~+2-3% tokens. Detailed experiment results linked in Links.
risks_mitigation: - Risk: over-rescaling might collapse dynamic range -> mitigate with clamp bounds and L2 regularizer in heuristic. - Risk: probe corpus not representative -> require sampling policy + fallback to default profile if sample entropy is below threshold. - Risk: runtime perf regressions -> fuse rescale into existing kernels and add microbenchmarks to CI.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged dev rollout on dedicated infra for internal tests. 2) Canary enable for 5 internal customers on dedicated capacity. 3) If metrics pass (accuracy regressions <0.5% and latency <5%), add to hosted model catalog as 'quant-profile-v2' optional. 4) Gradual default migration for models with stable profiles after two cycles of regression-free validation.
acceptance_criteria: - Probe runner implemented and able to produce per-layer profile JSON for each model family. - Runtime supports rescale hooks with fused no-op path. - Validation harness shows top-k overlap improvement or non-regression vs existing profiles on three test suites for Llama/Mistral/Qwen. - End-to-end perf P50/P99 within 1.1x of baseline for 95% of tests. - Docs + migration guide published.
